ardia apply.description:
Apply several tab and group operations in one call, in order, without touching the tab each window shows. Reads
JSON from FILE, or stdin with - or no FILE: a list of operations, or {"ops": [...]}. Every operation is checked
before the first one runs; a target that is gone or private stops the batch at that operation, and the reply says
which ones ran. An id may be $N: what operation N made (its group, else its tabs).

Operations (fields in docs/automation.md): open, tab.move, tab.pin, tab.unpin, tab.activate, tab.mute,
tab.unmute, tab.sleep, tab.wake, tab.close, tab.rename, tab.icon, group.create, group.update, group.move,
group.ungroup, group.close, group.delete.

Exit status: 0 done, 1 refused, a bad request or a target that isn't there (nothing after the failing operation
ran), 2 Ardia can't be reached (or the connection dropped after the request went out, so it may or may not have run).

Example:
  ardia apply <<'EOF'
  [{"op": "group.create", "urls": ["https://a.example", "https://b.example"], "name": "Research", "pinned": false},
   {"op": "group.create", "parent": "$0", "tabs": ["tab-7"], "name": "Papers", "icon": "📚"},
   {"op": "group.update", "group": "$1", "collapsed": true}]
  EOF

ardia call.description:
Send any method to the running Ardia over its control socket and print the result. Ardia's control socket reaches
the whole browser and every data point in the profile; `ardia methods` lists what this Ardia offers, with each
method's params, result and whether it changes anything.

Params come from --params (a JSON object, or - to read one from stdin) and -p (repeatable): -p key=value sets a
string, -p key:=value a JSON value (a number, true, null, an object or a list). -p wins over --params for the same key.

Params must be clean JSON: UTF-8, no lone surrogates, no NaN or Infinity, no number too large for a double, no key
twice, at most 64 levels deep, and not empty (send {} for no params). The whole request is at most 1 MB.

Exit status: 0 done, 1 Ardia refused or failed the method, 2 the params or options aren't valid (nothing was sent),
Ardia can't be reached, or the connection dropped after the request went out, or Ardia answered with neither a result
nor an error (so the method may or may not have run).

Examples:
  ardia methods
  ardia methods run
  ardia call windows --json
  ardia call run -p command=selectTab -p arg=3 -p window:=2
  ardia call run --params '{"command": "newTab"}'
  echo '{"command": "toggleSidebar"}' | ardia call run --params -

ardia feedback.description:
Report a problem or an idea to Ardia's developer: a confusing error, a missing command, output that cost you extra
turns, something slow. Give it a short title and say what you ran, what happened and what you expected.

It goes to the feedback service on ardia.dev (sent even while "Share anonymous crash reports and usage stats" is off:
sending a report is consent for that report). The service may publish the title and description as a public GitHub
issue, whatever the sharing setting; the reply prints the issue's link, or says none was opened. Files you attach stay
private. Before it leaves, secrets are removed by exact pattern (key=value and key: value secrets, auth
headers, known key formats, JWTs), along with emails, URL logins and queries, card numbers and the name in
/Users/<name>. At most 20 a day are sent. When it can't be sent, it's kept on this Mac and the reason is printed.
ardia feedback.epilog:
Examples:
  ardia feedback --title "snapshot -i hides dialog buttons" "the Save button inside a dialog wasn't listed with a ref"
  ardia feedback --kind slow --title "open takes 9 s" --command "ardia browse open https://example.com" "it used to take 1 s"
  echo "fill on a date input typed into the wrong field" | ardia feedback --title "fill misses date inputs"
  ardia feedback --title "click did nothing" --attach shot.png "the button stayed the same after click @e4"

Attach: .mp4 (one recording, 100 MB), .json.gz (one trace, 50 MB), .ips crash reports, and .png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp
.heic .mov .txt .log .md .json .jsonl .csv (10 MB each), 10 files at most.

ardia groups.description:
List and organize tab groups: create (around tabs you name, URLs you open, or one new tab), rename, set the icon,
colour and collapsed state, nest, reorder, pin, move to another window or profile, ungroup, close or delete. New
groups are pinned, as with New Group with Tab in the sidebar, unless --unpinned or --parent says otherwise. A group
made from tabs of another group, with no --parent, --before or --after, goes just above that group, so groups made
one after another from it keep their order and what's left of it stays below. A group argument takes an id or a
name, looked up case-insensitively in the last focused window (--parent: in the window the group goes to); an exact
id wins, and a name two groups share is refused with their ids.

Exit status: 0 done, 1 refused, a bad request or a target that isn't there (nothing after the failing operation
ran), 2 Ardia can't be reached (or the connection dropped after the request went out, so it may or may not have run).

Examples:
  ardia groups create tab-1 tab-2 --name Work --icon 🚀 --color blue
  ardia groups create --parent Work --url https://a.example --url https://b.example --name Reading
  ardia groups update Work --collapse --icon symbol:briefcase
  ardia groups move Reading --parent Projects
  ardia groups ungroup Imported

ardia on.description:
Run PROGRAM for each matching event, until interrupted. The event's JSON line is PROGRAM's stdin; its environment
has ARDIA_EVENT, ARDIA_WINDOW_ID, ARDIA_TAB_ID, ARDIA_PROFILE, ARDIA_URL and ARDIA_TITLE (set or removed for every
run; never a notification's text). PROGRAM runs directly, never through a shell unless PROGRAM is one; a leading ~
is expanded. URLs come without their query and fragment unless --full-urls. tab.idle, tab.resumed, user.idle and
user.active need --idle (like 30m, at least 1m).

--match takes userscript match patterns (https://*.example.com/*); any of them may match, and events without a URL
never match. One run at a time, at most 100 events waiting (the oldest are dropped, with a warning). A run is
stopped after --timeout seconds (default 60): SIGTERM, then SIGKILL 5 s later. When Ardia quits or control turns
off it reconnects with backoff.

Examples:
  ardia on tab.navigated --match 'https://*.youtube.com/*' -- ~/bin/yt-hook
  ardia on tab.opened,tab.closed -- /bin/sh -c 'echo "$ARDIA_EVENT $ARDIA_URL" >> ~/tabs.log'
  ardia on tab.idle --idle 30m -- ~/bin/park-tab
ardia on.usage: ardia on [-h] [--data-dir DIR] [--match PATTERN] [--timeout S] [--idle DURATION] [--full-urls] EVENT[,EVENT...] -- PROGRAM [ARGS...]

of the config folder (config-folder/plugins, or <data dir>/config/plugins with --data-dir or $ARDIA_DATA_DIR). Ardia sees

  install    copy a plugin folder (or a lone plugin.json) into the plugins folder
  check      check plugin manifests against plugin.schema.json
  remove     remove a plugin (through Ardia when it's running)
  enable     ask Ardia to show a plugin's consent sheet
  disable    turn a plugin off
  call       call one of a plugin's tools and print its result as JSON
  path       print the plugins folder

  opencode      ~/.config/opencode/skills   ./.opencode/skills

Next to each one it installs cua-driver's own skill (cua-driver, for computer use in native apps through
ardia computer), pinned to the bundled driver; --no-cua skips it. A cua-driver skill that ardia didn't install, from
cua's own installer for one, is left alone.

Installing or updating the CLI runs `ardia skills install --auto`: the skill goes to every coding agent found here
(Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode; general when none is), never over a folder ardia didn't write, and not again where
the user removed it.
Ardia remembers where it installed the skill, and each CLI update rewrites those copies (ardia skills refresh).

ardia tabs.description:
List and organize Ardia's tabs: the same actions as the sidebar, through the app's own store, so pins, groups and
sync behave exactly as when you do it by hand. Nothing here changes which tab a window shows unless you ask
(tabs open --activate, tabs activate) or close the tab it shows. Private windows are never reachable.

Without a command, it lists every window's tabs per profile: Top Apps, the pinned section (pinned tabs and pinned
groups), then the rest, with groups nested as in the sidebar. --json prints the tree with stable ids (see
docs/automation.md); --flat prints one tab per line.

--usage adds each tab's renderer process: its pid, CPU (percent of one core, as Chrome's Task Manager shows it) and
memory, hottest first, so a process from `top -o power` or Activity Monitor can be named. --pid N prints the tabs
running in process N. With --json each tab gets "pid", "cpu" and "memory" (bytes); null for a sleeping tab, which has
no process. Tabs that share a process show that process's numbers. The first --usage in a while takes about 2 s,
since CPU is measured over time.

Ids: tab-… for tabs, g-… for groups, w-… for windows (ardia tabs shows them). --group takes a group's id or its
name (case-insensitive, in that window; an exact id wins, and a name two groups share is refused with their ids).
--before and --after take a tab or a group id.

Exit status: 0 done, 1 refused, a bad request or a target that isn't there (nothing after the failing operation
ran), 2 Ardia can't be reached (or the connection dropped after the request went out, so it may or may not have run).

Examples:
  ardia tabs --json
  ardia tabs --usage
  ardia tabs --pid 61234
  ardia tabs open https://example.com news.ycombinator.com --group Work
  ardia tabs move tab-1 tab-2 --group Work
  ardia tabs move tab-3 --top
  ardia tabs pin tab-4 --row
  ardia tabs sleep tab-5 tab-6

ardia theme.description:
Themes live in <config folder>/themes/NAME.json: a "dark" and a "light" block of colour roles, and "type"
(fonts, text sizes, weights), "metrics" (row heights, sidebar width, corner radii), "layout" (sidebar parts to
hide or move) and "icons" (SF Symbols to swap). Every key is optional; a block left out is Ardia's own look.
config.json's "theme" picks one; saving the active theme restyles Ardia at once.

Colours: #RGB, #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA, rgb(r,g,b) or rgba(r,g,b,a) (r, g, b 0-255, a 0-1). grain and the ...Opacity
roles take numbers 0-1, the ...Radius roles 0-100, tabSelectedBorder a list of two colours. Ranges and defaults
for the other blocks are in theme.schema.json; ardia theme check reports each bad key in Ardia's words.

Commands:
  new NAME [--from THEME]   write themes/NAME.json with every role and look key (never overwrites)

      { "name": "fresh-tab", "on": "app.launched", "command": "newTab" },
      { "name": "standup", "at": "09:55", "days": ["mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri"], "run": ["~/bin/standup"] },
      { "name": "old-reddit", "on": "tab.opening", "rewrite": [{ "match": "https://www.reddit.com/*", "to": "https://old.reddit.com{path}{query}" }] },
      { "name": "jira", "omnibox": { "title": "Jira", "keyword": "j" }, "run": ["~/bin/jira-suggest"] }

run like ardia on (see ardia on --help); command hooks run an Ardia command in the event's window and tab; decide
hooks (tab.opening, link.opening, download.deciding, permission.requested) answer before Ardia acts, as rules
Ardia applies itself or as a program whose stdout is the answer; scheduled hooks get a schedule.fired event.

Ardia's Settings › Advanced › Automation. run re-reads hooks.json when it changes; an invalid file keeps the hooks
loaded before. Output goes to ~/Library/Logs/Ardia/hooks.log (rotated at 5 MB). See docs/automation.md.

ardia hooks.description:
Run hooks from hooks.json in the config folder (${ARDIA_CONFIG_HOME:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}}/ardia/config, or <data dir>/config with
--data-dir or $ARDIA_DATA_DIR) in one process:

  {
    "hooks": [
      { "name": "yt-to-media", "on": ["tab.navigated"], "match": ["https://*.youtube.com/*"],
        "run": ["~/bin/yt-hook"], "timeout": 30, "fullUrls": true },
      { "name": "fresh-tab", "on": "app.launched", "command": "newTab" },
      { "name": "standup", "at": "09:55", "days": ["mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri"], "run": ["~/bin/standup"] },
      { "name": "old-reddit", "on": "tab.opening", "rewrite": [{ "match": "https://www.reddit.com/*", "to": "https://old.reddit.com{path}{query}" }] },
      { "name": "jira", "omnibox": { "title": "Jira", "keyword": "j" }, "run": ["~/bin/jira-suggest"] }
    ]
  }

A hook has one trigger (on, at, every or omnibox) and one action (run, command, or a decide answer). Event hooks
run like ardia on (see ardia on --help); command hooks run an Ardia command in the event's window and tab; decide
hooks (tab.opening, link.opening, download.deciding, permission.requested) answer before Ardia acts, as rules
Ardia applies itself or as a program whose stdout is the answer; scheduled hooks get a schedule.fired event.
Rules that route or rewrite links, pick folders, run decide programs or read the address bar wait for approval in
Ardia's Settings › Advanced › Automation. run re-reads hooks.json when it changes; an invalid file keeps the hooks
loaded before. Output goes to ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/ardia/hooks.log (rotated at 5 MB). See docs/automation.md.

Commands:
  run         run the hooks until interrupted
  install     run them at login: a systemd user service (dev.ardia.hooks.service) that keeps ardia hooks run alive
  uninstall   remove the systemd user service
  list        the hooks in hooks.json and whether the systemd user service runs

ardia scripts test.description:
Build FILE, open a background tab of its own, register the script at document start, open the page, and report.

The script runs where its @match/@include rules say, at its @run-at point, in the top frame and (without @noframes)
every iframe, cross-origin ones included. The report lists the script's own console output and uncaught exceptions
(with positions mapped back to your source files), errors the page threw itself, whether it ran in the top frame
and in iframes, and the --expect value. After the script ran and the page loaded, the test listens for --wait seconds (Chrome
reports an unhandled promise rejection about a second late), retrying --expect (a JavaScript expression, awaited,
in the page's world) until it's truthy. The tab closes at the end unless --keep.

@inject-into content runs in the page's world here (ardia command connections can't create isolated worlds), with
a warning.

Exit status: 0 the script ran without uncaught exceptions and --expect was truthy, 1 otherwise (build error, the
page didn't match, an exception, a falsy --expect), 2 Ardia can't be reached.
